doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Ben Webster's sound and Buddy Rich's drumming
summary: The smoky 52nd Street atmosphere, guests who sat in with Rich's band, and Rich as the Art Tatum of drums.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Really. That’s a good story, kind of that romantic, semi-funky atmosphere.
Yeah. The smoke is filling the air and he’s playing, I don’t remember what tune, but that sound and everything.

Wow. That’s what I wanted to do. I remember a few times we had different people sit in with us with Buddy’s band, like Erroll Garner sat in and a lot of the drummers, Philly Joe Jones and Mel Lewis and Ed Shaughnessy, and I can’t think of some of the other guys, Joe Morello. But Philly Joe sounded so good. But Buddy of course was, he’d wipe them all out with his things. I used to call him the Art Tatum of the drums, because you know he could just do anything, it was fantastic. You used to hear 20 minute drum solos practically every night for two years, and beautiful. He had such great control of everything.
